items.q: A publisher uses an SSP to sell its ad space to many buyers.
items.why: The SSP connects the publisher’s inventory to many buyers at once.

items.q: An SSP can connect a publisher to many DSPs at the same time.
items.why: Several DSPs can bid on the same impression through the SSP.

items.q: An SSP can only work with one ad exchange.
items.why: SSPs commonly connect to many exchanges and buyers.

items.q: A header bidding wrapper and an SSP are always the same product.
items.why: A wrapper is code that collects bids in the page. An SSP is a platform that can be one of the bidders it calls.

items.q: An SSP can apply the floor prices a publisher sets.
items.why: Bids below the floor are not allowed to win.

items.q: An SSP can help a publisher block unwanted advertisers or categories.
items.why: Publishers can set blocks for brands, sectors and sensitive categories.

items.q: Sellers.json is a public list of who sells through an ad platform.
items.why: Buyers use it, with ads.txt, to check who is behind an impression.
